negative_results.claim: The current @relation candidate creates a separate backend-neutral lexical relation namespace while retaining the existing @ref syntax unchanged.
negative_results.observed: LALR contextual accepted 5/7 combined cases and LALR basic 3/7; Earley dynamic accepted 7/7. Existing standalone @refs and ref operands caused LALR regressions. Non-colliding sigil control and quoted generic relation call were 7/7 across all three modes.
negative_results.scope: This does not refute sigils in general, a redesigned disjoint @ form, declared relation registries, or a generic canonical Relation node.
negative_results.next_falsifier: Real frozen BASE parser full-corpus cross-backend proof with stable roundtrip hashes and no diagnostics/cost regression.

negative_results.claim: A relation-only parser corpus is sufficient to establish compatibility of a new relation token class with the existing ClayCode language.
negative_results.observed: The prior @relation run was 8/8 on relation forms but omitted existing @ref coexistence. Adding refs exposed parser-mode-dependent failures.
negative_results.scope: General lesson for CC-WP-02: new token classes must be tested against all overlapping existing lexical classes and mixed-context roundtrips, not only positive feature examples.
negative_results.next_falsifier: A static lexer-overlap checker plus complete corpus mutation suite proves feature-local tests cover all overlapping token classes.
